newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, PGMs aided by strike.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, PGMs aided by strike.

text.p: The precious metals markets made a tentative start to the week on Monday having witnessed a change of government in France and gold take centre stage in a high profile political row in Germany in the past few days.

The arrival in Tokyo of Russian platinum group metals (PGMs) export agency officials to open long delayed formal talks on 1997 export contracts with Japanese importers was overhsadowed by a one-day strike in South Africa as a price influence, dealers said.
Gold fixed easier at $344.00 per ounce, down $1.60 from Friday when bullion closed at $344.40/$344.90 which was followed by losses in New York and the Far East.

Dealers forecast the change to a socialist government in France under Lionel Jospin giving up the austerity programme aimed at getting France into the European Monetary Union (EMU) at the first pass in 1999.
"The election result could lead to a delay in the Euro start up and that is providing some psychological support for gold," one dealer said.

The German government's insistence that the Bundesbank revalues its gold reserves and the bank's rejection of the plan last week, could weaken if not delay EMU, by weakening the entrance criteria, economists said.
Broker GNI said in a commentary, "While the French vote puts more pressure on EMU, the net effect is likely to be a stronger U.S. dollar which is negative for gold."
A 24-hour strike called by South Africa's biggest labour federation Cosatu affected production at many of the country's precious metal mines.
That was background news for gold but more significant for the PGMs as it countered to some extent the arrival in Tokyo at the weekend of Almaz officials to agree export contracts.
Platinum at $404.00/$407.00 a couple of dollars firmer and palladium at $180.00/$183.00 was also $2.00 up on Friday.
"We have seen the highs in the PGMs for now but they will stay very volatile," a dealer said.
Silver was unchanged at $4.73/$4.75 but dealers noted that the forward rates were tightening.
The market late on Thursday before the July Nymex conract lost over 16 cents on Friday.
"The buying seemed to anticipate the fund selling we saw on Friday in New York. Silver could be the next one to watch," one dealer said.
